channel.title: Nature Communications
channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: [8] Field-angle-resolved heat transport in UTe2: determination of nodal positions in the superconducting order parameter
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: P. J. Hirschfeld, Johnpierre Paglione

Authors: Ian M. Hayes, Elliot Fang, Shanta R. Saha, Vivek Mishra, P. J. Hirschfeld, Johnpierre Paglione

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental characterization of gap symmetry in the high-profile unconventional superconductor UTe2.

Tags: #UTe2 #superconductivity #transport

Abstract: Determining the gap symmetry of superconducting phases in UTe2 remains a central challenge. Here, the authors use field-angle-dependent thermal conductivity and theoretical analysis to identify b-axis point nodes in the low-field state, consistent with a B2u order parameter.

item.title: [6] Constructing radiative dipolar excitons via frontier-state hybridization in 2D perovskites
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Ti Wang, Hongxing Xu

Authors: Jiakai Yan, Cheng Wang, Siyi Wu, et al.

Score 6/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Study of excitonic properties in 2D materials, relevant to broader quantum materials research.

Tags: #2Dmaterials #excitons #perovskites

Abstract: Dipolar excitons offer long-range interactions but typically suffer from weak optical activity. Yan et al. engineer frontier-state hybridization in a two-dimensional perovskite to realize optically active dipolar excitons with long-range repulsive interactions.

item.title: [7] Deep strong light-matter coupling in 3D Kane fermions without Dicke criticality
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Wojciech Knap, Marcin Białek

Authors: Dmitriy Yavorskiy, David Hagenmüller, Noureddine Charrouj, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant topological semimetal physics and light-matter interaction study.

Tags: #topological #semimetal #light-mattercoupling

Abstract: In the deep-strong light-matter coupling regime, the interaction strength exceeds the frequencies of uncoupled light and matter excitations. Here, the authors access the deep-strong-coupling regime in mercury cadmium telluride and report a single-mode coupling ratio of 1.6 above room temperature.
